2_Introduction: The devices exhibited an increased PCE from 19.053% to 19.053%, with a VOC of 1.1138 V, FF of 72.5059%, and JSC of 23.594 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor is Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the second step, 160 µL of chlorobenzene was dropped on the spinning substrate 6 s before the end of the process. After the spin coating was completed, it was annealed on a hot stage at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ perovskite composition—featuring a mixed A-site cation cocktail—enhances phase stability and suppresses δ-phase formation by optimizing the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), while the partial Br⁻ substitution at the X-site widens the bandgap slightly and mitigates halide segregation under operational stress; its crystallization kinetics are critically governed by the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) enabling uniform wet-film formation and precursor redistribution, followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) inducing rapid solvent evaporation and nucleation onset—where the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL chlorobenzene introduced 6 s before spin termination) triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation density and suppressing Ostwald ripening, thereby yielding compact, pinhole-free films with enlarged grain boundaries and reduced non-radiative recombination centers; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min facilitates complete solvent removal, lattice relaxation, and defect healing—particularly at undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites and halide vacancies—while avoiding excessive volatilization of FA⁺ or MA⁺ that would otherwise induce phase impurity or interfacial voids. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional and processing design achieves interfacial and bulk defect control through synergistic cation entropy stabilization, halide lattice stiffening, and kinetic confinement of crystal growth—evidenced by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks in XRD (indicating full conversion and negligible residual lead halide), high film coverage and uniform grayscale intensity across optical micrographs (confirming morphological continuity and suppressed shunt pathways), and strong, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence with prolonged decay lifetimes (reflecting suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative yield); collectively, these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic signatures underpin robust charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and balanced carrier transport—yielding VOC = 1.1138 V, JSC = 23.594 mA/cm², FF = 72.5059%, and PCE = 19.053%.
